title: I started making an idle game after leaving my old studio
author: DeadCatCreative
selftext:
I was able to get pretty far in my career because of my creativity, so rather than let my anxiety eat me alive after leaving my old studio, I did the only thing I could think of and I started making a game. Of course I'm hoping it'll do well commercially, but really I'm just trying to keep my skills up to date and prove something to myself.

I already had ChatGPT, and I’d spent a few months learning Codex while my previous studio was starting to integrate AI into its workflow. So I hooked the project up through MCP, grabbed a few Unity assets, and started building. I began with a pretty robust building system, then started layering in systems from an idle template I picked up for about $25

It’s still early so a lot of what you’re seeing is foundational work, but getting this far has alread. My confidence as a designer had taken a pretty brutal hit, and working on this reminded me why I love making games in the first place.

Tools:

Miro - create mockups in frames, export to PDF, feed that to GPT/Codex; organize visual references

ChatGPT/Codex - identifies design gaps, makes suggestions to improve design clarity, gathers analytics, and more

comments.author: West_Satisfaction299
comments.body: I like how its look so far. What's the theme of it?

replies.author: DeadCatCreative
replies.body: The core narrative theme is 'A safe, lively little tavern at the edge of a dangerous fantasy world, run by cats' but that's subject to change this early on 😅
